description: A DX7 operator envelope on its own: a voice is read from a cartridge file, its carrier envelope taken, and played as a 0-10V envelope from a gate, with an offset on each of its eight stage settings

params.text: Picks the patch whose carrier envelope is used
Picks which loaded bank the patch comes from
Shifts that stage's rate, -99 to 99 added to the patch's own figure; a rate is a speed rather than a time, so higher is faster
Shifts that stage's level, -99 to 99 added to the patch's own figure, clamped to the DX7's own 0 to 99 range
Shifts the voice's own tremolo speed
Shifts how long after the note starts the tremolo fades in
Shifts how deep the tremolo is
Shifts how sensitive the carrier is to the tremolo, 0 to 3; tremolo needs this, the depth and the rate all above zero

inputs.text: A rise starts the attack and a fall starts the release
Picks the patch, 0-10V across the voice slots, added to the voice knob
Picks the bank, one volt per bank, added to the bank knob
Shifts that stage's rate, ±5V across the whole offset range
Shifts that stage's level, ±5V across the whole offset range
Scales the envelope's speed with pitch the way the DX7 does, so a note higher up the keyboard gets a faster envelope
Scales the envelope output, 0-10V added to the output level knob
Shifts the tremolo speed, ±5V added to the LFO knob
Shifts the tremolo depth, ±5V added to the depth knob

notes: the envelope has four rates and four levels rather than attack, decay, sustain and release: it ramps to each level in turn, holds at the third under the gate, then moves to the fourth
because neighbouring levels in a DX7 patch are often equal and the rates saturate, a small offset sometimes makes no audible difference; that is how the original behaves
menu: Release to 0V — ends the release at 0V rather than at the patch's own fourth level
Banks — a label over the bank items below it
Load bank (.syx)… — reads a thirty-two voice DX7 cartridge file, which is then kept with the patch
Remove current bank — drops the selected bank; it appears only once more than one bank is loaded
LFO waveform — a label over the waveform choices below it, which set the shape of the tremolo: From voice, Triangle, Saw down, Saw up, Square, Sine or Sample & hold
